input.justification: The variable `param` is set to a user-controlled HTTP header name (from `request.headers.keys()`), and is assigned to `bar` via a conditional expression that does not sanitize it in the true-positive case (the condition `(7*42)-num>200` with num=106 evaluates to false, so `bar = param` is always taken at runtime). `bar` is then concatenated directly into a file path `fileName = f'{TESTFILES_DIR}/{bar}'` which is passed to `open()`. There is no path normalization, allow-listing, or removal of traversal sequences (e.g. `../`) anywhere in this flow, so an attacker can supply a header name containing `../` sequences to read arbitrary files outside the intended directory. This matches the classic OWASP Benchmark path traversal pattern and is a genuine vulnerability.
